searchText: PR makes sense to me, we can implement when merged I was exploring a design that exploits the near-100% redundancy of validators in the beacon state storage. A sort of validators sector, with structural sharing https://dev.to/galadd/cutting-beacon-state-storage-by-97-validator-sectors-with-structural-sharing-3p5c Kindly give it a read, and let me know what you think of the approach So is the main realization here that deposits come mostly in large batches? No, but that if you take 2 full beacon states validators, depending on the time between them, nothing really changes between them. As little as ~0.01%. Wasteful to then have checkpoints for archival storage with that much redundancy (technically almost 100%) Nimbus has done at least part of this (haven't checked all), the refactoring out of the immutable parts of the validators, going back to ... Altair? Bellatrix? rather than storing them in each state Yes, the idea is that main storage is separate from how we point to that storage. It doesn't matter the phase, so it goes back to them. I'll check out how Nimbus goes about it All that will be stored in each state will be a list of "pointers" Yeah but this is already exploited in clients for storage At least Prysm and Lighthouse already ship state diffs. But we don't exploit the clustering of deposits That's nice. I'll take some time to check all out Wdym by clustering of deposits Deposits usually come in batches, pools make large deposits at once. This means there are long stretches with not that many changes on the validator slice and then suddenly we get periods with a lot of new entries. I thought you meant to exploit this situation for better storage I did see clusters of changes in my data, but my assumption was that that is solved by having 64 validators per chunk. (not necessarily solved. just that it means it favors my design). But now, upon closer inspection, maybe there's something to actually look into here. Will think about it. it's because of the entry/exit churn rate quotas nothing for a while, then the quota fills, then it stops, repeat

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: So is the main realization here that deposits come mostly in large batches?

excerpts.author: gbolahan
excerpts.content: No, but that if you take 2 full beacon states validators, depending on the time between them, nothing really changes between them. As little as ~0.01%. Wasteful to then have checkpoints for archival storage with that much redundancy (technically almost 100%)

But now, upon closer inspection, maybe there's something to actually look into here. Will think about it.
